target_customer: Engineering teams at large enterprises with heavy codebase maintenance
problem: Engineering teams spend a large share of time on migrations and upgrades; the company first sold AI feature creation then refocused on migrations.
business_model: SaaS with free tier for small repos and Pro tier for larger codebases
product_category: AI codebase migration and maintenance agents

founders.name: Eric Rowell
founders.background_notes: Author of HTML5 Canvas Cookbook; later co-founded Wayline (YC S25).

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable automated migrations across large enterprise codebases needed scanners, dependency resolvers and hand built blueprints, hard for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Migration modules are hand built but replicable; established tools such as OpenRewrite based products and general coding agents covered the same jobs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents acquiring or copying Second specifically; general AI coding agents later covered migration tasks.

market_need_then: Second's own relaunch post cites hundreds of discovery conversations and a claim that large companies spend about half their engineering time on maintenance; three large enterprises were said to be using it.

branding.domain_note: Uses second.dev, a .dev domain, not an exact .com

brand_strength.rationale: The name was framed as a second developer bot in the founder's launch post, but no press, community or logo evidence was found.

pivots.from: AI feature creation for commodity web apps (a second developer bot)
pivots.to: AI enterprise codebase migrations and upgrades only
pivots.why: Founder says discovery conversations showed codebase maintenance was a bigger pain at large companies.

outcome_analysis: Second is listed Inactive by YC and its founder is shown as a former founder who moved on to Wayline in 2025. The cause is not public. It raised a small $1.9M pre-seed, pivoted once to migrations in a crowded space, and the failure factor is a tentative reading of that pivot, not a stated reason.
notes: Pre-seed date conflicts: Caplight and the YC page say 2024-06, VCBacked says 2023-04. The cause of inactivity is not public; exit type left unknown because YC Inactive does not state shutdown. Competitor entries are undated directory or press pages, flagged as such. Several searches returned other companies shutting down; none concern Second. Grit.io (founded 2022 per a directory) and Moderne (OpenRewrite based) were in the migration space but no source dated near March 2023 was found, so the competitor list is empty.
